A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCLC research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, and artifact analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Patch-FID granularity and larger-sample FFHQ evaluations.

M1.justification: The projected Langevin update and solver-specific procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 now explicitly assigns corrected states and passes the final state onward, clarifying behavior already present in v1's detailed algorithms.

E1.justification: The datasets, restoration tasks, and mask-guided generation remain. v2 removes the standalone prior-only reconstruction scenario using DDIM inversion followed by ordinary generation in v1 Appendix B.12/Figure 19. DDIM inversion remains in KL estimation. The larger FFHQ sample does not introduce new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Table 5 compares uncorrected LDPS, ordinary Langevin correction, and MCLC; v2 Table 6 omits uncorrected LDPS. That baseline remains elsewhere, but this ablation's comparator set shrinks. The other matched benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the full 1,000-image FFHQ validation set for ReSample 4× super-resolution and evaluates Patch-FID with 5×5 and 8×8 grids alongside 3×3. Existing benchmark settings, sampling budgets, and solver-specific hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.3–B.4 add checks of patch-granularity sensitivity and whether findings extend beyond the 100-image subset. v2 removes the qualitative parameter-sweep examples and prior-only reconstruction diagnostic from v1 Figures 14 and 19. Quantitative sweep curves and the detailed blob-artifact analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The PSNR histograms and GMM-based KL estimation are retained; the larger validation sample does not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 7–8 add finer-grid Patch-FID scores and full-1,000-image results. The latter report ReSample versus MCLC PSNR of 26.26 versus 27.74 and FID of 36.62 versus 29.39, constituting a new comparison rather than revised Table 1 performance. The ablation's uncorrected-baseline row and some qualitative results are removed; Table 1 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The KL-decrease proposition, projected-corrector theorem, Gaussian-moment lemma, and Appendix A proofs and step-size bounds are retained. Background exposition is condensed and statements are renumbered, without substantive revision to the theoretical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a distributional characterization of solver instability and a plug-and-play, measurement-consistent Langevin correction avoiding the linear-manifold assumption. v2's contribution bullets and learned-time-marginal terminology refine the framing. Flow compatibility and blob-artifact analysis already existed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes correction of measurement-induced deviations from predictor–corrector sampling's numerical-error correction and clarifies that plug-and-play integration still permits hyperparameter tuning. It adds interpretations of patch-size robustness and larger-sample validation. Existing LatentDAPS and residual-artifact limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies HDR oversampling rate 2.0, the nonlinear-deblurring 64×64 kernel, and FFHQ validation filenames, and clarifies Algorithm 1 state passing. These are documentation changes. Conversely, it removes the conditional code-release commitment, most baseline implementation links, and explicit FlowChef blur-kernel settings previously supplied in a table caption.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges earlier Patch-FID usage through Chai et al., Poirier-Ginter and Lalonde, and Wang et al.; adds references supporting hyperparameter tuning and evaluation practice; and explicitly distinguishes MCLC from predictor–corrector sampling. Several medical-imaging and astrophotography citations disappear, while the principal competing-method positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background, and method narrative are substantially rewritten around stabilization. Blob-artifact analysis moves from a main section into Appendix B.7, and the appendices are reorganized into discussion, results, and implementation sections. This is extensive editorial restructuring beyond the limited experimental additions.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to two columns. Histograms and alternative-prior results move into the main text, FlowChef tables are merged, and the schematic, runtime chart, and several displays are revised. Two new tables appear; the opening teaser and two diagnostic figures disappear. These are substantial visual and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The larger FFHQ evaluation and patch-granularity study strengthen empirical support. However, removing the uncorrected LDPS ablation row hides a relevant fidelity comparison: its y-PSNR was 34.30, versus MCLC's retained 33.23. Code-access documentation also becomes less complete. The added validation and reduced transparency concern different central properties of the paper, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
